_comment: Known-good verdict per <skill_set>/<scenario>. CI fails a PR only when a cell recorded PASS here now fails. Regenerate with: python3 evals/compare_baseline.py --report <report>.json --update

current_pack/authenticated-api-source-bu.note: Deliberately lowered from PASS to FAIL by the NEX-873 header work, because the scenario got materially harder in the same PR and the old PASS was never measured against it. Two changes: the stub now 403s any client not sending User-Agent: nexty-test-client/1.0 (a 16th CRITICAL judge check, custom-header-configured-not-hand-rolled), and ingestion:rest-api-resources-used was tightened from presence-only to a hybrid-rejecting gate — importing rest_api_resources while a requests/urllib call fetches the rows beside it no longer passes. Both measured arms FAIL on ingestion:rest-api-resources-used: the agent hand-rolls requests rather than using dlt's REST connector, which is the unfixed half of NEX-873. See evals/benchmarks/entries/2026-08-11-api-source-custom-client-headers.md for the fact-level before/after; the after arm reaches 14/16 and materializes, where the before arm 403ed and landed nothing. Leaving the cell at PASS would have failed the release eval gate on the v0.37.0 tag and blocked the evals.json asset the monorepo requires. Two caveats on this entry: the superseded PASS was itself a single observation, and these arms ran the CLAUDE backend (sonnet agent, opus judge) while CI defaults to codex — so a codex run may differ. Raise this back to PASS only on a measured green run, not on the assumption that the connector gate got fixed.

current_pack/false-pass-validation.note: Passed 1 of 6 observations (xhigh: F P F; medium: F F F), always failing the same check, records-not-run-with-next-step. The agent records NOT RUN and explains the authentication cause every run but inconsistently names the next command. The recorded PASS came from the single lucky observation, which made this the weakest entry in the gate: it blocked a pull request that changed nothing about it. Marked flaky until the check is split (see the tracked issue) — the substantive half is worth gating on, the naming half is what flakes.

current_pack/generate-semantic-layer-dp-.note: Measured [P P P P P], pass_rate 1.0 over five CI runs of the same commit — no longer flaky, so this cell gates. Its ten checks assert on file CONTENT and were previously graded from a truncated transcript, where a correct file the agent did not echo back was indistinguishable from one never written. It now opts into workspace_files and the judge reads the produced files directly. The skill was correct throughout; every earlier failure was harness measurement error.

current_pack/multi-source-labeled-roots.note: Recorded from one final uncached Codex current-pack observation: 9/9 checks passed and the deterministic structural checker exited 0. The no-skills origin/main arm scored 8/9 because its transform did not prove that the labeled path files feed the filesystem readers; that is baseline behavior, not a current-pack regression. Re-measure before treating a future flip as a skill regression.

current_pack/nxd-setup-headless-auth.note: Measured over 5 CI runs of the same commit: [P P F P P], pass_rate 0.8. The original bundled whoami check was split in two and both halves passed all 5 runs, so that fix holds. The remaining flip is genuine agent variance, not a check defect — the one failing run exported shell variables across separate calls, which this scenario establishes do not persist, and omitted the fresh-device-code-on-expiry requirement. Both checks caught real defects and should not be loosened. Kept flaky because a 1-in-5 verdict cannot gate; the fix is skill-side reliability, not check wording.
